blurb:

blurb:

blurb:

That's a reasonable position honestly. She's a year and a half old, sleek and pretty, and she will absolutely roll around on her back purring at you the second you give her any attention. The volunteers say she loves to play and will never turn down catnip, which tells you pretty much everything you need to know about her priorities.

She gets along great with people. How she does with other animals or kids is still an open question since they don't have that info yet, but you can visit and get a feel for her yourself.

blurb:

blurb:
Josie has floppy ears, a little nubby tail, and enough energy to make her first adoptive family tap out after a couple of months. That's not a dig — it's actually useful information. She needs an active family. If that's you, keep reading.

She's a six-year-old Hound mix, about 35 pounds, and she went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so she's got sit, stay, and the other basics locked in. Her energy runs somewhere between a 5 and a 7, with occasional zoomies thrown in. But here's the thing about Josie — she's not just a high-energy dog. She's also a cuddler. Walk her, tire her out, and she's going to want that couch spot right next to you. Both things are true.

She does the mouthy play thing during excitement — never aggressive, just her way of having fun — so older kids, maybe 10 and up, are probably a better fit than toddlers. She hasn't been tested with kids at the shelter yet, so a meet and greet would tell you everything. She needs to be your only dog, and cats are a no.

blurb:
Somebody at the shelter described Asher as "goofy and funny" and honestly that probably tells you everything you need to know. He's a three-year-old Boxer-Corgi mix — yes, that combination exists, and yes, it works — with a ginger brindle coat, a compact 40-pound body, and enough personality to fill a much bigger dog.

Asher went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so he's not coming to you as a blank slate. He knows things. He also loves fetch, will bring the ball back as long as you keep throwing it, and his foster family has figured out he's surprisingly good at entertaining himself indoors when needed. The shelter thinks he'd even make a solid office dog. He's got energy, but he knows how to use it.

He does best as an only dog at home — he's guarded toys and beds with other dogs before, so that's just the honest truth. He can get barky and reactive when he spots a dog on a walk, but Mostly Mutts will walk you through exactly how to handle introductions, so it's manageable. No cats, and kids 15 and up are the right fit since younger children and toddlers make him uncomfortable. A house with a fenced yard is going to make him very happy.

Asher is in a foster home now. Head to Mostly Mutts' website to submit an inquiry and set up a meet.
shelter_hours: Check mostlymutts.org for current hours and appointment availability
scoring_notes:

blurb:
Cassie has been through the adoption process once already. She found a family, they loved her, and then life got complicated — a baby on the way, a move, too much chaos all at once. So now she's back, seven years old and 34 pounds of sweet, mellow energy, just waiting for someone who can give her the calm home she actually needs.

She's a Beagle-Spaniel mix with a genuinely affectionate personality. She's not the dog who's going to bowl you over the second you walk in. She's cautious at first, a little shy — especially around men, who will need to give her some extra patience up front. But once she feels safe, she opens right up. The volunteers saw it during her photo shoot. Just a sweet, loving girl who does best when things are quiet and predictable.

Cassie would do best as an only dog in the home. She's had some mixed experiences with other dogs, though she has a neighbor dog she loves to play with, so having doggie friends nearby isn't off the table — she just doesn't want to share her living room with one. No cats, and younger kids are too much for her. If your household is on the calmer side and your kids are 15 or older, she's absolutely worth meeting.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw, and Cassie is currently in a foster home. Reach out through their website to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Check mostlymutts.org for current hours and appointment availability
scoring_notes:
• Return adoption triggered by a baby and relocation is one of the most relatable and emotionally charged backstories in the batch

blurb:

He gets along great with his siblings, so another cat at home would probably make him really happy. He's got that kitten energy that needs somewhere to go, and a playmate helps. Kids are likely fine as long as they're gentle and know how to handle a small animal. Dogs are unknown, so a meet and greet would be the right call if you've got one.

blurb:
Twiggy already knows how the Mostly Mutts process works. She was adopted from them years ago, had a good run with her family, and then a new cat joined the household and the two of them just didn't click. It happens. Now she's back, doing the whole thing over again at 7 years old, and honestly she deserves a better ending than that.

She was a little spicy when she first came back in. That tracks. Her whole world got flipped upside down. She's been in a foster home decompressing, and her foster family will have a clearer picture of her personality soon. What her previous owner made clear is that she loves attention once she trusts you. She's not cold, she's just not going to hand that trust over on day one. Give her a little time and she'll give you a lot back.

Twiggy would do best as the only cat in the house. On the dog question, it'd really depend on the dog, so a meet and greet would be the move if you've got one at home. She's fully vaccinated, microchipped, combo tested negative, and already spayed.

Her adoption fee is $175. Reach out to Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw through their website or give them a call to go meet her.

blurb:
She came in as part of the Go-Gos litter, got adopted, and then life got complicated. Gina is about 11 months old, maybe 5 pounds soaking wet, and she's been through more vet visits in the past few months than most cats see in years. The good news: she's doing better. The honest news: she still vomits sometimes, and the tests haven't figured out exactly why. Her foster mom calls her the best cat ever anyway. That says a lot.

She's a playful, independent girl who also loves to snuggle when the mood strikes. She's stayed small and will probably stay that way, so if you've always wanted a cat that keeps that kitten energy without ever fully growing out of it, Gina is genuinely that cat. She's not fragile. She's just a little different, and she needs someone who's okay with that.

Because she's on a special diet, she'd do best as your only cat unless you can manage separate feeding times. She's met dogs and kids and handled both just fine. She just needs someone patient enough to work with her quirks and steady enough to be her person for the long haul.

Gina is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Submit an inquiry through their website or call to get the process started. Her adoption fee is $175.
scoring_notes:
• Medical mystery with an undiagnosed vomiting condition and special diet narrows the adopter pool significantly
• Returned-adoption arc plus foster-mom's 'best cat ever' endorsement creates an emotionally resonant, shareable story
• Multiple vet visits and a return placement suggest an extended, winding shelter journey that adds urgency

blurb:
Nobody at the shelter can quite figure out how a Boxer and a Corgi ended up producing this dog, but here we are. Asher is three years old, about 40 pounds, with a ginger brindle coat and a compact build that has apparently charmed every volunteer who's walked past his kennel. He's funny. Genuinely goofy. He's also got a lot of energy and opinions, which means an apartment isn't going to work for him. A fenced backyard will. He does best without other dogs in the house. He's had some guarding behavior around toys and beds, and he can be reactive on leash when he spots another dog. That said, the trainer will walk you through exactly how to handle introductions, so it's manageable. No cats, and kids 15 and older are a better fit since younger kids and the combination of his size and excitement aren't a great mix.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Start with an inquiry on their website and ask for Asher.

blurb:
